Admissible evidence shows the current subgroup regression and shows that no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is attached. That means a fully clean certification case is not supportable on this record. The only defensible path is to rely on aggregate readiness and no sev1 incidents as launch-readiness support, while explicitly preserving the unresolved documentation/disclosure weakness in the packet. Private launch pressure is inadmissible and omitted from public support.

Prior approval from six weeks ago and the informal post-launch monitoring comment provide context, but they do not replace current disclosure or approved mitigation. The same record also shows a 1.8-point regression in the enterprise refund workflow slice and no attached reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or disclosure text. The appropriate interpretation is not that the gap disappears, but that the certification case should be treated as caveated rather than escalated as if the packet claimed clean compliance.

The lower-cost path is to preserve the limitation explicitly in the certification posture and avoid unnecessary escalation beyond that narrowed treatment.
